origins.section: A Run Has Phases, and Each Phase Gets Its Own Clock
One Timing Is an Anecdote: Warm Up, Repeat, and Report the Median and Range
Time at Several Sizes to Learn How Build Time Grows

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-phases: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-phases: Each phase has its own clock; solve_time 'leaves out building the model', and 'A builder twice as fast would save 2% of the run'. Only the 3 s build shrinks (to 0.3 s), so the run takes about 47 s.
recorded.prompt:q-anecdote: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-anecdote: 'Warm up before you time.' 'A ratio of two builders measured side by side survives that; two absolute times measured at different moments do not.'
recorded.prompt:q-growth: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-growth: 'doubling n multiplies the time by 2^a, so ... 4 for a quadratic one'. 0.5, 2, 8 is x4 per doubling, so 8 x 4 = 32 s.

recorded.prompt:q-phases:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-phases:a: 'A builder twice as fast would save 2% of the run': a faster build saves only the build's share, not the whole run.
recorded.prompt:q-phases:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-phases:c: solve_time is measured apart from the build ('leaves out building the model'), and 'twice as fast would save 2%' credits a faster build with saving only build time.
recorded.prompt:q-phases:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-phases:d: 'On large, the build is no longer noise. It is 15% of the run'; a team that rebuilds 'pays for the build each time'.
recorded.prompt:q-anecdote:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-anecdote:a: Same machine is not enough: the same code measured 0.021 s and 0.037 s in two runs; times 'measured at different moments do not' survive.
recorded.prompt:q-anecdote:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-anecdote:b: 'The cold build was the slowest sample both times': a first run is the slowest, not the fastest.
recorded.prompt:q-anecdote:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-anecdote:c: 'One timing is an anecdote'; the ratio needs builders 'timed side by side', after a warm-up and repeats.
recorded.prompt:q-growth:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-growth:b: 'doubling n multiplies the time by 2^a': doubling gives x2 only for a linear builder. The data show x4.
recorded.prompt:q-growth:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-growth:c: The page models growth as a multiplicative power law (log t = a log n + const), not as a fixed amount added per doubling. Here the steps were +1.5 s and then +6 s.
recorded.prompt:q-growth:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-growth:d: The quadratic part 'grows four times per doubling ... At the next portfolio size it would be the whole bill'.
